Priya K.: Hey folks — hitting an install failure on my M1 Mac when installing redwoodctl v0.9.2 via Homebrew. `brew install redwood/redwood/redwoodctl` fails with a weird permissions/arch error. Anyone seen this?

Alex M.: Can you paste the full error? Did you try `brew update && brew upgrade` first?

Priya K.: Full excerpt below:
```
==> Installing redwoodctl from redwood/homebrew
==> Downloading https://github.com/redwood/repo/releases/download/v0.9.2/redwoodctl-darwin-amd64.tar.gz
Error: Permission denied @ rb_sysopen - /usr/local/bin/redwoodctl
ld: symbol(s) not found for architecture arm64
```
also `brew doctor` suggests my Homebrew is at /opt/homebrew but the formula looks like it tries /usr/local.

Sam T.: Sounds like a mismatched bottle / old Homebrew path. On Apple Silicon you should be using /opt/homebrew. Two workarounds that helped me:
1) `arch -arm64 brew install --build-from-source redwoodctl`
2) Download the universal binary tarball from releases and `tar -xzf` into `/opt/homebrew/bin`

Priya K.: `arch` trick worked, thanks Sam. Repro notes: fresh macOS 13, migrated Homebrew at /opt/homebrew, had stray /usr/local symlinks. Might be worth adding an M1 note in the install docs.

Evan L.: FWIW I hit a separate issue when testing login/profile behavior. If your `~/.redwood/config.toml` contains multiple `[profile]` sections with the same `name` (happens after some merges), `redwoodctl login --profile team-a` sometimes writes the token under the wrong profile key. Repro: create two sections `name = "team-a"` with different `url` and run `redwoodctl login --profile team-a` — token ends up in the first matching table, not the one matching both name+url.

Alex M.: Oof. That sounds like the parser is doing a naive append/merge and ignores explicit `--profile`. Can you open a bug with the config and a minimal repro? This would explain a lot of CI flakes.

Priya K.: Filed issue #2324 with logs and reproducer. Workaround for now: export `REDWOODCTL_PROFILE=team-a` before `redwoodctl login` or edit `~/.redwood/config.toml` to dedupe the profile sections.

redwoodctl-bot: New issue created: #2324 — "redwoodctl: login uses wrong profile when config contains duplicate profile sections" by Priya K. https://github.com/redwood/repo/issues/2324

Sam T.: Another local-dev gotcha: `redwoodctl dev --local` will try browser SSO if `REDWOOD_API_KEY` isn't set. In headless CI that hangs forever. We should support `--no-browser` or accept `--token` via stdin for non-interactive flows. I'm prepping a docs PR.

Alex M.: We do have `--token` in newer builds, but it's not documented in older release notes. If you open a small PR to patch the dev docs and mention `export REDWOODCTL_PROFILE` workaround we can ship it in the next docs patch.

Evan L.: One more note on auth retries: CLI retries auth 3x with exponential backoff, but concurrent CI logins can still trigger SSO rate limits. Suggest adding tunables: `--retries`, `--backoff-ms`, and an env like `REDWOODCTL_MAX_CONCURRENT_AUTH=1` to limit parallel auth attempts. I'll add to the issue.

Priya K.: Thanks everyone — adding the M1 install note and the REDWOODCTL_PROFILE workaround to the onboarding doc now.

Sam T.: :thumbsup:

Alex M.: I'll include the profile merge fix in the 0.9.3 changelog and bump the Homebrew formula to build from source for arm64 if we can't get a universal bottle out fast.
